idiom_name: emitted .d.ts as the published interface plus non-exported implementation
implementation_notes: TypeScript has a literal header/implementation split: tsc --declaration emits .d.ts files that are the interface consumers compile against while the implementation stays in .js or .ts behind the package's exports map, and /** @internal */ together with stripInternal (or API Extractor's d.ts rollups) trims members that must not appear on that surface. Inside the module, keep the body unnameable with non-exported declarations, #private class fields or closures, and let a factory return an interface or an opaque branded type instead of the implementation type. The classic pointer wrapper is only worth writing when the body must be swapped at runtime behind a stable factory function.
pitfalls: stripInternal is documented as an internal compiler option to use at your own risk - the compiler does not check that the result is valid, so an internal type that still appears in a public signature leaves dangling declarations and consumers see broken or any-typed APIs; API Extractor or an api-report test is the real guard.
@internal, private and protected are erased at runtime: only #private fields and closure state are enforced, so anything that must be protected at runtime has to use those.
Shipping the .ts sources instead of compiled output plus declarations hands the implementation to consumers and makes declaration trimming cosmetic.
